full_judgment:
3. It appears that Aftaf Hossain was a refugee from India and he was allotted the aforesaid house by the Deputy Commissioner, Relief and Rehabilitation on 14-3-1966 and directed him to deposit Taka 568.00 in favour of the Government. Accordingly, he deposited the said amount by chalan dated 30-3-1968. Petitioner claimed that since such allotment she had been living in the said house with her husband who died on 12-2-1985 leaving behind his legal heirs including the petitioner and since then petitioner and other heirs of late Altaf Hossain are living in the said house. After the death of Altaf Hossain, an application was filed by the petitioner and other heirs of Altaf Hossain to the Government for finalisation of the allotment in their favour. Thereafter, on 25-5-1988 aletter was issued to the petitioner and other heirs of Altaf Hossain to produce their allotment letter, chalan showing depositing Taka 568.00 and other documents on 31-5-1988. Accordingly, they appeared and produced the same before the appropriate authority but the matter was not disposed of and on 13-2-1992, petitioner came to learn that the said house has been enlisted as an abandoned house. So she filed an application to the Court of Settlement which was registered as case No. 23/92 and by judgment dated 3-12-1992 the said case was rejected as barred by limitation. Thereafter petitioner moved this court and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. It appears that aforesaid house in question has been included in the 'Ka' list of abandoned houses published in the Bangladesh Gazette Extraordinary dated 23-9-1986 under the provisions of section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985. Unless possession of a house is taken over by the Government that cannot be included in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings. In view of the same we are of the view that inclusion of petitioner's house in the 'Ka' list of abandoned houses is without any lawful authority. Petitioner's application before the Court of Settlement was not dismissed on merit, rather on the ground of limitation. 

 6. Right to hold property is a fundamental right under Article 42 of the Constitution. Enlistment of a house in the list of abandoned buildings under the provisions of section 5 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance 1985 is not violative of the aforesaid fundamental right to hold property by a citizen if the same falls within the mischief of abandoned property under President's Order 16 of 1972. Treating one's property as abandoned property under President's Order 16 of 1972 and inclusion of the same in the list of abandoned buildings when the house does not fall within the mischief of abandoned buildings violates fundamental right of such a person to hold property. Though the petitioner is in possession of the house from the time of her allottee husband treating the same as abandoned property and inclusion of her house in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings is not only contrary to the provisions of President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and Ordinance 54/85 but also violative of her fundamental right to hold property. In such circumstances petitioner is entitled to challenge the inclusion of her house in the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings in the writ jurisdiction of this court in spite of dismissal of her application by the Court of Settlement on the ground of limitation. Had no fundamental right of the petitioner been violated dismissal of her case on the ground of limitation by the Court of Settlement would not have entitled her to challenge the inclusion of her house in the list of abandoned houses without challenging the order of the Court of Settlement.
